settings.title: Settings
settings.secret_keep_placeholder: Leave blank to keep the current password
settings.secret_is_set: A password is set. Leave blank to keep it.
settings.pxe_server_ip_helper: Address of this node that PXE clients load the netboot.xyz boot files from (TFTP). Prefer a static address.
settings.dynamic_warning_desc: This address can change when the node reboots, which would silently break network boot. Choose a static address or reserve this one in your DHCP server.
settings.proxy_dhcp_on_desc: Your router keeps assigning IP addresses; this node only adds the boot information for machines that network boot, with the right file for BIOS, UEFI, Secure Boot and ARM64. Every machine in this network that tries PXE boot will get the netboot.xyz menu. Do not run another PXE server in the same network. Leave the DHCP options 66/67 on the router empty.
settings.router_options_desc: proxyDHCP is off, so your DHCP server must point clients here. DrayTek Vigor: LAN > General Setup > DHCP Server Option. Option 66 (TFTP server): {ip}. Option 67 (boot file): {uefi} for UEFI machines or {bios} for legacy BIOS. Most routers, including DrayTek, can serve only one boot file for all clients; enable proxyDHCP to handle BIOS and UEFI machines automatically.
settings.uefi_boot_mode_helper: Secure Boot uses the Microsoft-signed shim and the iPXE-signed binaries, so machines can boot with Secure Boot enabled. Its menus are always loaded from boot.netboot.xyz.
settings.web_section_desc: Optional. The netboot.xyz web app edits the boot menus and upgrades the menu version. It is protected with a login; PXE boot works without it.
settings.host_helper: Fully qualified host name of the web app. Leave empty to disable the web app route.
settings.admin_user_invalid: Use 1-64 letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore
settings.admin_password_helper: At least 8 characters. Anyone with this login can change what every PXE client on your network boots.
settings.admin_password_required: Set a password to publish the web app
settings.ip_allowlist_helper: One network (CIDR) per line. Only these clients can reach the web app. Leave empty to allow all.
settings.invalid_cidr: Enter networks in CIDR notation, e.g. 192.168.1.0/24
settings.pxe_server_ip_not_on_node: This address does not belong to this node
settings.domain_already_used_in_traefik: This host name is already used by another application
